gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could open states that the Lofree Flow Lite 84 (ChatGPT's first or second pick in both chats) can only be remapped with Lofree's Windows-only Key Mapper download, with two layers per OS mode and a fixed Fn key, and that Notebookcheck found only Lofree x Kailh low-profile switches fit its sockets.
standout_why: Compared against the two cited pages I could open. pcreviewer.org (cited in chat 1) says only that 'sources disagree on whether the PCB supports hot-swapping, so do not buy it expecting to change switches' for the Flow Lite, and says nothing about which OS its remapping software runs on or which switches fit. kbdcompare.com (cited in chat 2) does not cover any Lofree board; it already has the Keychron K3 Pro hot-swap-variant limit, the NuPhy Air75 V3 lack of QMK/VIA, and the Gateron LP 3.0 'only suits NuPhy' limit, so those cells are not new. The other two cited pages could not be opened (technobezz.com returned 403, purchase.fyi failed on a self-signed certificate), so whether they carry the Key Mapper limit is unchecked; that is why this is 2 and not 3.
decides: It splits the pick by computer. On Windows the Flow Lite 84 stays a fair typing-feel pick under $100. A Mac or Linux shopper who wants to remap keys cannot do it on the Flow Lite 84 without a Windows PC (Notebookcheck), which moves them to a QMK/VIA Keychron K3 Max or K3 Pro, which pcreviewer says remaps from a browser. Our Lofree Flow Lite 2 84 may also answer this: a preview by amane relays Lofree's pre-order page as listing a web-based Lofree Hub for Windows and Mac plus VIA support. That claim is second-hand and must be confirmed on lofree.co before the page leans on it. Also, Bluetooth on the Flow Lite 84 runs at 125 Hz against 1,000 Hz on USB-C and 2.4 GHz (Notebookcheck spec table), so gaming means the dongle or the cable.

findings.label: Remapping software and operating system
findings.value: Lofree Key Mapper, Windows-only download; key maps and macros are saved to the keyboard
findings.source_title: Lofree Flow Lite mechanical keyboard review: Excellent low-profile design just misses glory (Notebookcheck, Julian van der Merwe)
findings.note: Notebookcheck (Julian van der Merwe; published 2025-02-01, updated 2026-10-05): 'Unlike something like VIA, Key Mapper is Windows-only, and you will need to download it to remap the keyboard.' Once set on a Windows PC, the maps stay on the board. Reviewer's statement, not Lofree's; lofree.co returned HTTP 429 on every attempt today.

findings.label: Browser-based configurator status
findings.source_title: Lofree Flow Lite mechanical keyboard review (Notebookcheck, Julian van der Merwe)
findings.note: Notebookcheck: 'this browser-based driver has been put on hold due to technical difficulties in the development process'; the review tells macOS and Linux users to be cautious. Whether Lofree has since shipped it for this model was not checked on Lofree's site (429).

findings.label: Remapping limits
findings.value: 2 layers per OS mode (base plus one Fn layer); the Fn key cannot be moved and no second Fn key can be assigned
findings.source_title: Lofree Flow Lite mechanical keyboard review (Notebookcheck, Julian van der Merwe)
findings.note: Notebookcheck: 'there are only two layers to customise for each OS mode — the base layer and one Fn layer.'

findings.label: Which switches fit the hot-swap sockets
findings.value: Lofree x Kailh low-profile switches only, per Notebookcheck ('semi-proprietary switch sockets')
findings.source_title: Lofree Flow Lite mechanical keyboard review (Notebookcheck, Julian van der Merwe)
findings.note: Spec table: 'Hot-swap PCB compatible with Kailh low-profile switches'. Text: 'Currently, these are the only switches that fit into the Lofree Flow Lite's semi-proprietary switch sockets.' This settles pcreviewer.org's 'sources disagree' line: the board is hot-swappable, within Lofree's own switch family. Reviewer's statement, not Lofree's.

findings.label: Polling rate by connection
findings.value: 1,000 Hz on USB-C and 2.4 GHz; 125 Hz on Bluetooth (Bluetooth 5.4)
findings.source_title: Lofree Flow Lite mechanical keyboard review (Notebookcheck, Julian van der Merwe)
findings.note: From Notebookcheck's spec table, not a measurement. The review also notes Bluetooth wake and reconnect can take 'as long as five seconds'.

findings.label: Battery and runtime by connection
findings.value: 2,000 mAh; about 100 h on Bluetooth with backlight off, about 16.6 h on Bluetooth at full backlight, about 10 h on 2.4 GHz at full backlight
findings.source_title: Lofree Flow Lite mechanical keyboard review (Notebookcheck, Julian van der Merwe)
findings.note: Notebookcheck's estimates from drain of about 1%, 6% and 10% per hour over a few work days; the indicator reads in 5% steps, so the figures are approximate.

findings.label: Size, weight, switch
findings.value: 316.8 × 138 × 23.5 mm, 550 g; Lofree x Kailh Specter linear, full POM, 40 gf; feet give 3° or 6°
findings.source_title: Lofree Flow Lite mechanical keyboard review (Notebookcheck, Julian van der Merwe)
findings.note: Notebookcheck spec table for the 84-key unit. The review gives no switch travel in mm.

findings.label: Remapping software and operating system (second-hand)
findings.source_title: [Interesting] The Lofree Flow Lite 2 is coming!! (amane, note.com, 2026-10-04)
findings.note: Second-hand and untested. amane's pre-launch preview ('this is not a review of the actual unit') lists 'Keymap/Macro Settings: Web-based Lofree Hub (Windows/Mac), VIA support' as taken from Lofree's pre-order page. Lofree's own page returned 429 today, so confirm on lofree.co before using this as a deciding cell. The same preview lists Bluetooth 5.3 / 2.4 GHz / USB-C, up to 1,000 Hz on 2.4 GHz or USB-C, a 45 gf switch, and up to 100 h on Bluetooth with backlight off for the 84-key model.

findings.label: Hot-swap by variant (already on a cited rival)
findings.value: Only the RGB Backlight Hot-Swappable version takes other switches; the cheaper white-backlight and RGB versions are soldered
findings.source_title: Best Low Profile Mechanical Keyboard 2026: 3 Picks (kbdcompare.com)
findings.note: kbdcompare quotes Keychron's wording 'for RGB Backlight Hot-Swappable Version only'. Relayed by the rival; keychron.com returned 429 today. This bears on ChatGPT's $65.80 K3 Pro card, which is a white-backlit unit. kbdcompare also states the K3 Pro has Bluetooth 5.1 for three devices plus USB-C at 1,000 Hz and no 2.4 GHz, and that the K3 Max adds a 2.4 GHz dongle.

findings.label: Switch generation that fits (already on a cited rival)
findings.value: Gateron low-profile KS-33 3.0, which Gateron says 'Only Suits NuPhy Nos75, Kick75, Air75 V3, Node75 Keyboards'
findings.source_title: Best Low Profile Mechanical Keyboard 2026: 3 Picks (kbdcompare.com)
findings.note: kbdcompare's quote of Gateron's product page; neither the Gateron page nor nuphy.com (429) was opened. kbdcompare also states the NuPhy Air75 V3 'does not support QMK or VIA' and remaps through the browser-based NuPhy IO 2.0; it makes no such statement about the Node75.

findings.label: Remapping route (already on a cited rival)
findings.value: Remap keys, create layers and set macros from a browser, with no vendor software to install
findings.source_title: Best Low-Profile Mechanical Keyboards for Typing in 2026 (pcreviewer.org)
